problem: processStartIdentity can return null for a live owner when /proc or ps identity lookup is unavailable; treating null as dead can reclaim a live mutation lock and violate single-writer durability

reviews.why: A null identity is ambiguous. Reclaim only when independent PID liveness proves the process is gone; preserve PID-reuse reclamation when a verifiable identity differs.

options: fail closed for live unverifiable owners
reviews.winner: fail closed for live unverifiable owners
reviews.why: Stealing a live lock can create concurrent writers and lost updates. Timing out is safer than violating the single-writer invariant.

options: local liveness callback plus existing identity check
reviews.winner: local liveness callback plus existing identity check
reviews.why: Adds no Qubes/network round-trips, no new service, and only one local process-liveness check on the ambiguous identity path.

qa: live owner with matching identity is never reclaimed
live owner with unavailable identity is not reclaimed and acquisition times out
dead owner with unavailable identity is reclaimed
reused PID with a different verifiable process identity is reclaimed
failures_lessons: Process identity lookup failure is not equivalent to process death.
Stale-lock recovery needs separate answers for liveness and identity equality.
Fail-closed lock contention is preferable to silent concurrent durable writers.
scope: Mission/runtime Slice 1 only; no Qubes transport, iPhone, calibration, or financial side effects
